note: Tags name the activity that practices the skill. Each bot supports practice toward a standard; it never claims to meet or cover it. Code text is copied from the official C3 Framework PDF (NCSS, rev. 0617). USCIS test content is the official federal question list, not a standards framework.
not_tagged: Symbols, holidays, geography and most American history recall questions carry no C3 tag: a recall drill does not practice the C3 history skills (sourcing, chronology analysis), so tags were dropped rather than stretched. D2.His.1.6-8 (shown as a candidate on the curriculum Page) was dropped for this reason.

standards.text: Explain specific roles played by citizens (such as voters, jurors, taxpayers, members of the armed forces, petitioners, protesters, and office-holders).
standards.activity: Rights and responsibilities questions (roles of citizens: voting, jury service, taxes, military service)

standards.text: Analyze the role of citizens in the U.S. political system, with attention to various theories of democracy, changes in Americans’ participation over time, and alternative models from other countries, past and present.
Examine the origins, purposes, and impact of constitutions, laws, treaties, and international agreements.
Explain the powers and limits of the three branches of government, public officials, and bureaucracies at different levels in the United States and in other countries.
Explain the origins, functions, and structure of government with reference to the U.S. Constitution, state constitutions, and selected other systems of government.
Explain multiple causes and effects of events and developments in the past.
standards.activity: American history questions that ask why something happened
